messages.author: c91a208fffacfb7e
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Blank line following \end{knitrout}
parts:
Thanks, Yihui. I think, in retrospect, that adding \noindent
explicitly in the .Rnw file when I don't want a new paragraph will be
easier after all.

On Wed, Aug 8, 2012 at 12:12 PM, Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Yes, you can remove the blank line after \end{knitrout}, but even you
> do that, the following text is still a separate paragraph in default
> knitr LaTeX output. Here is how to do it (set the 'document' hook to
> replace '\end{knitrout} '):
>
> \documentclass{article}
>
> egin{document}
>
> Knitr replaces exttt{@} with an empty string so that it becomes a
> blank line in the tex output.
>
> <<setup>>=
> knit_hooks$set(document = function(x) {
> gsub('(\\end\{knitrout\}) ', '\1', x)
> })
> @
>
> See if it works.
> <<>>=
> # hello world
> 1+1
> @
> This line should continue as a part of the above paragraph instead of
> a separate paragraph.
>
> \end{document}
>
>
> This is due to the kframe environment (anything after it becomes a new
> paragraph). If you want the Sweave style, you can simply use
> render_sweave() (it will set all the options you mentioned). But at
> the moment, there is a tiny problem that I need to solve (will do it
> soon).
>
> That said, an alternative way to solve this problem is to add
> oindent automatically, e.g.
>
> knit_hooks$set(document = function(x) {
> gsub('(\\end\{knitrout\}[ ]+)', '\1\\noindent ', x)
> })
>
> Regards,
> Yihui
> --
> Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
> Phone: 515-294-2465 Web: http://yihui.name
> Department of Statistics, Iowa State University
> 2215 Snedecor Hall, Ames, IA
>
>
> On Wed, Aug 8, 2012 at 11:49 AM, Douglas Bates <dmb...@gmail.com> wrote:
>> My global opts_chunk contains tidy=FALSE, prompt=TRUE, comment='' because I
>> would like to reproduce Sweave-style chunks. I find that there is a blank
>> line following the knitrout environment in the .tex file I produce so that
>>
>> <<lm1>>=
>> lm1 <- lm(log(conc) ~ sqrt(age), PCB)
>> @
>> Model-fitting functions in \proglang{R} produce an object of a
>>
>> becomes
>>
>> egin{knitrout}
>> \definecolor{shadecolor}{rgb}{0.969, 0.969,
>> 0.969}\color{fgcolor} egin{kframe}
>> egin{alltt}
>>> lm1 <- \hlfunctioncall{lm}(\hlfunctioncall{log}(conc) ~
>>> \hlfunctioncall{sqrt}(age), PCB)
>> \end{alltt}
>> \end{kframe}
>> \end{knitrout}
>>
>> Model-fitting functions in \proglang{R} produce an object of a
>>
>> Is there a way to suppress that blank line? I would prefer not to need to
>> add oindent when I want the text following the knitrout environment to
>> continue the paragraph.
>>

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Blank line following \end{knitrout}
parts:
Someone brought up this issue again after two years, and I just fixed
it :) (https://github.com/yihui/knitr/commit/2b52194e) There will no
longer be blank lines inserted after code chunks, unless you
intentionally insert some.

> \end{knitrout}
